conviction_note: The evidence is balanced. US staffing series (SIA/Bullhorn hours +9% YoY to late September, ASA +3.3%) back the guide's strongest region. France (August PMI employment still falling, Synergie flagging a French slowdown) and Italy (September composite down to 51.0, hiring near stagnant) weigh on the Q4 guide the stock trades on. The +10.8 put skew and a 9.5% short interest cut opposite ways. So p_up is 51 on a 9% absolute move and the findings sum to about zero. The two measurements agree that there is no edge.
bar: Company Q3 guide: adj EPS $0.96-1.06 (midpoint $1.01), reported revenue +2% to +6% on Q3 2025's $4.6bn (about $4.72-4.91bn, midpoint about $4.82bn), CC +3-7%, organic days-adjusted CC about +6%, adj EBITA margin 2.1-2.3%, tax 44% (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/manpowergroup-man-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/ ; regional ranges per https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/manpowergroup-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-16/). Street EPS is $1.01-1.03, at or just above the guide midpoint. Street revenue is $4.85-4.92bn, above the guide midpoint (Benzinga and Earnings Whispers via search, https://earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/MAN/202606). The EPS bar is sourced to the company guide and two agreeing estimate sources. The revenue bar sits about 1-2% above the guide midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,426,985 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, about 9.5% of 46.51m shares outstanding, 5.38 days to cover. It peaked at 6.75m on 2026-06-30, fell 1.45m in the July squeeze, and has held flat at 4.4-4.9m since mid-August, so shorts did not rebuild into the print (https://equibles.com/stocks/man/short-interest, read 2026-10-14). Baseline: 25-delta skew +10.83 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.98, ATM IV 116.9%, event-implied move 8.5%. Spot $51.57 is -10.98% over 20 days, -2.46% over 5 days, -18% from the 52-week high and +100% from the 52-week low. The stock has de-rated into the print while the short base is moderately large: a squeeze mechanism exists on a good guide, and the skew says the market is paying for a guide disappointment.

findings.finding: US commercial staffing volumes ran well above a year ago through the end of Q3. The SIA/Bullhorn Staffing Indicator for the week ending 2026-09-26 shows US staffing hours +9% YoY (commercial +11%, industrial +15%, professional +8%, office/clerical -8%) at a year-to-date high. ASA's index for 7-13 September was +3.3% YoY, after +5.5% YoY in mid-August. MAN guided US Q3 growth 'similar to Q2' (8% organic days-adjusted, Manpower US +16%), so this independent series supports the US line printing at or above the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: US +8% organic and Manpower US +16% drove the beat-and-guide print that moved +32.37% (baseline; https://www.rttnews.com/3667730/manpowergroup-stock-surges-32-after-returning-to-q2-profit.aspx). Q4 2025 (Jan 2026 print) US recovery commentary: +14.95%.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell 11% over 20 days with put skew bid, which looks like the market weighting the weak BLS temp-help headline (finding 2) over the private hours series. If the market had priced the hours data, the 20-day tape would not show a de-rating into a quarter whose largest growth driver is tracking ahead. Caveat: the US is about a sixth of revenue, and the index is a sample of Bullhorn-using firms, not MAN.
findings.independence: ASA Staffing Index, week of 7-13 Sep 2026, +3.3% YoY (https://americanstaffing.net/research/asa-staffing-industry-data/staffing-index/). This is a different source pointing the same way. It contradicts the BLS series in finding 2.

findings.finding: BLS temporary-help employment fell 10,900 in September 2026 (the year's largest drop), July was revised to -10,000 and August to +200. That is about -20,700 over Q3 sequentially, against a headline payroll gain of only +29k and unemployment of 4.2%. It is a public macro negative for US staffing volume and for the tone of the Q4 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: October 2025 print: beat, but management said US demand was 'slowing further' and guided Q4 soft, and the stock fell -6.52% (baseline; https://business.dptribune.com/dptribune/news/read/43307230/manpowergroup_sees_demand_for_jobs_%E2%80%98slowing_further).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is a widely read BLS headline from 2 October and coincides with the stock's 20-day slide. It stays as a small negative because management will be asked about it on the call and could talk Q4 down. Snippet only (403 on fetch); figures come from SIA's summary of the BLS release.
findings.independence: Same SIA data, and SIA says Sept temp-help employment is still 35,400 above December 2025, so the year-on-year level is positive. It conflicts with the Bullhorn and ASA series in finding 1. The two are different measures (a payroll level versus sampled hours), so both are filed and they partly offset.

findings.finding: France, MAN's largest European market (guided Q3 'flat to slight growth' after flat CC in Q2), is softening. INSEE puts Q2 2026 temp employment at -1.0% QoQ and -1.7% YoY. The HCOB France composite PMI was 48.5 in August, the eighth month of contraction, with employment falling again. Peer Synergie said on 2026-09-23 that French revenue 'marque le pas' (is stalling) with a Q2 slowdown and took a cautious H2 stance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Southern Europe and France softness drove the weak Q4 2025 guide at the October 2025 print (-6.52%) and the April 2025 guide cut (-19.07%) (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: French temp data and the Synergie H1 release are published but rarely read by US holders of MAN. Consensus revenue still sits above the guide midpoint, which would not be the case if a France shortfall were priced. Shrunk because MAN France held flat in Q2 while the INSEE series fell 1.7% YoY, so MAN has been outperforming its market. Its France guide already implies no growth, so a miss here is small. What has to go right elsewhere: the US and Italy, about two fifths of revenue, are tracking at or above guide.
findings.independence: INSEE IR214 (https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/9039152) and HCOB France PMI August (https://tradingeconomics.com/france/composite-pmi/news/580849, 2026-09-03). Three different sources, filed as one finding.

findings.finding: Italy, MAN's strongest European market in Q2 (+6% days-adjusted CC, guided low-to-mid single digit for Q3), lost momentum at the end of the quarter. The HCOB Italy composite PMI fell to 51.0 in September from 53.6 in August, and private-sector hiring slowed to 'near-stagnant' after August's fastest job growth in over two years. The risk is to Q4 commentary rather than to Q3 revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean Italy-specific reaction in the baseline. Southern Europe weakness fed the -19.07% April 2025 guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a macro survey released 5 October and not company-confirmed. If priced, Southern Europe revenue estimates would have been trimmed, and there is no sign of revisions. This is a proxy, so it is kept small.
findings.independence: Italy manufacturing PMI 50.4 in September, with job creation continuing (https://investinglive.com/news/italy-september-manufacturing-pmi-50-4-vs-50-0-expected/), which partly cuts against it. Otherwise none.

findings.finding: Peers that spoke after MAN's 16 July guide said Q3 started better. Randstad (22 July) reported Q2 organic +1.9% against about 1% consensus, said the majority of markets were in growth with volumes improving further into July, and named Southern Europe as a growth driver. Synergie (23 September) said its international business grew 13.6% with especially strong momentum in Southern Europe.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When peers and MAN both showed stabilisation (the Jan 2026 and Jul 2026 prints), the stock rose +14.95% and +32.37% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Randstad's July read is nearly three months old and largely priced. Synergie's late-September Southern Europe comment is fresher and little read in the US. A stock 11% off in 20 days is not pricing a Q3 that tracked ahead of the 6% organic guide.
findings.independence: Synergie H1 release via BFM/Zonebourse (https://www.tradingsat.com/synergie-FR0000032658/actualites/synergie-synergie-l-international-porte-la-croissance-la-france-marque-le-pas-1170665.html). It shares that document with finding 3, but this finding uses its Southern Europe and international lines, not France.

findings.finding: MAN's own Employment Outlook Survey for Q4 2026 (8 September) shows the global Net Employment Outlook at 29%, +2 points QoQ and +6 YoY. The US is at 36% and Europe/Middle East rose 5 points to 22%. This is the company's own forward hiring read and suggests management will frame Q4 constructively.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no measured reaction to the survey itself. Constructive Q4 guidance framing in January and July 2026 coincided with large positive reactions (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and widely syndicated, so mostly priced. It is kept small because the stock has fallen since, which suggests the market discounted it against weak September macro data. Hiring-intention surveys predict revenue only loosely.
findings.independence: Same company document syndicated via https://finviz.com/news/389720/global-hiring-outlook-strengthens-for-q4-as-workforce-transformation-drives-demand-for-new-skills. No independent source.

findings.finding: The revenue bar is above the company's guide. Street revenue is $4.85-4.92bn against a guide midpoint of about $4.82bn (reported +2-6% on Q3 2025's $4.6bn), while Street EPS of $1.01-1.03 sits at or just above the $1.01 midpoint. A print at the guide midpoint reads as a small revenue miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 2026: an in-line print moved +0.88%. October 2025: a beat on EPS with soft revenue moved -6.52% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: This is the bar itself, so it is priced by definition. It is filed because the bar is above the company guide midpoint and the gap tilts the read of an in-line print slightly negative.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 revenue base of $4.6bn from the company's 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/871763/000119312525240850/man-ex99_1.htm). Benzinga cites $4.85bn.

findings.finding: Positioning is set up for upside asymmetry if the guide holds. Short interest has held at 4.4-4.9m shares (about 9.5% of shares outstanding, 5.4 days to cover) since mid-August without rebuilding. The stock is -11% over 20 days and -18% from its high, and the July print showed a 1.45m-share cover inside two weeks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: short interest of 6.26m shares (15 July) met a beat and guide and the stock moved +32.37%. Short interest fell to 4.81m by 31 July (equibles).
findings.why_not_priced: The put skew (+10.8) prices downside. A 20-day de-rating with an unchanged short base means expectations have been reset lower while the squeeze fuel is still in place. This runs against the skew, and the reason given is that the de-rating already reflects macro fear that the company-level US data does not confirm. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: Baseline tape: run_up_20d -10.98%, skew +10.83 (sealed baseline file). It cuts against the skew.

findings.finding: EUR/USD weakened late in Q3, to roughly 1.148 on 2026-09-21 from about 1.16 in early September, against a Q3 2025 average near 1.17. That is consistent with the guide's -$0.02 FX assumption, with at most a cent of extra translation headwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean FX-driven reaction in the history. FX is guided explicitly and looked through.
findings.why_not_priced: Public FX data, essentially priced, and inside the guided FX headwind. Filed for completeness.
findings.independence: Currency Beacon 9 Sep: USD/EUR 0.8598, which implies about 1.163 (https://currencybeacon.com/rates/USD/EUR).

outside_window.finding: Synergie Q3 2026 revenue (French staffing peer, the first Q3 read on French temp volumes) is due 21 October after the close.
Randstad Q3 2026 results, scheduled 22 October per AJ Bell's calendar.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR since 2026-07-16: only an 8-K item 5.02 (Paychex CEO John Gibson added to the board, effective 1 Sep), S-8 POS amendments, 13Gs, and a Form 3/4 on 2026-09-03 tied to the board appointment. No insider selling cluster, no financing, no pre-release.
Analyst rating or target changes dated September-October 2026: none found with a verifiable date.

Q3 2026 peer pre-releases or prints (Randstad, Adecco, Robert Half, Kelly, Kforce, Synergie): none have reported yet. Their July guides only (Robert Half Q3 revenue $1.31-1.41bn, Kforce sequential growth).
Prism'emploi national July and August 2026 barometer: not yet published or indexed (latest is May, +0.5% YoY).
September 2026 France flash PMI level: only a teaser headline ('activité positive en septembre') with no number.
Company divestitures or acquisitions after Jefferson Wells US: none.

rejected_candidates.detail: This is already in the 10-Q filed 2026-08-07 and has no bearing on the Q3 print or guide. It is a known balance-sheet item, not a new fact. The source page date could not be verified (bot wall).

rejected_candidates.candidate: Earnings Whispers lists the report on 2026-10-19
rejected_candidates.detail: The company press release of 2026-10-01 confirms 2026-10-15 before the open (https://finviz.com/news/397869/manpowergroup-to-announce-3rd-quarter-2026-earnings-results).

baseline_tension: Mixed. The US staffing data and the steady short base cut against the +10.8 put skew and the -11% 20-day slide. The France and Italy macro softening agrees with them. Net, nothing here beats the option market.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broad series): the Bullhorn hours sample cut from +0.8 to +0.6 against the broader BLS series, and BLS cut from -0.5 to -0.4 because its year-on-year level is still positive.

Lessons 5 and 9 (company number beats proxy; size a segment net of the rest): France cut from -0.8 to -0.6, because MAN France was flat while the INSEE market fell 1.7% in Q2 and its guide already assumes about zero growth.
Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew): the positioning long cut from +0.5 to +0.3, with the reason the option market may be wrong stated in why_not_priced.
Core 3c and lesson 3 (caveats move p_up toward 50): p_up moved from 52 to 51.
